Broadband Deployment Program (BDP)


Broadband Deployment Program (BDP, ARPA CPF) 

Through the ARPA CPF Broadband Deployment Program, approximately $139 million in Capital Projects Fund resources are being invested to expand reliable, high-speed, fiber optic broadband service to unserved and underserved locations throughout Oregon, with a strong emphasis on affordable access to essential online services.


BDP (ARPA CPF) News & Updates

United States Department of Treasury Approves
Project Buildout Extensions for ARPA Capital Project Fund

On August 28, 2026, Oregon Broadband Office (OBO) received the fully executed grant agreement amendment from the U.S. Treasury. Extensions were requested for 14 projects, allowing broadband infrastructure projects currently underway an additional 6 months to reach completion. Read the full press release here for more details.

Awardees can access the BDP Subrecipient Resources webpage for next steps, and consult the BDP Program Handbook (PDF) for complete guidance.

Application Phase: Eligibility
Eligible Applicants:
The following entities are eligible to apply for funding through the ARPA CPF (BDP) Program:
  • Municipalities (as defined in ORS 285B.410(9)). 
  • Private and for-profit entities
  • Electric utilities
  • Co-operatives
  • Municipal affiliates (economic development corporations, regional planning and development councils, and councils of government) 
  • Nonprofit organizations
  • Partnerships between eligible applicants
Note:  All applicants for Program funding must have authority for their proposed Project. For example, while ports are generally eligible applicants as they are included within the definition of municipality, ORS 777.271 limits the authority of rural ports to acquire certain telecommunications infrastructure or facilities and to provide certain telecommunications services.

Eligible Projects:
The sole eligible activity for this Program is the construction and deployment of Broadband Infrastructure Projects (“Projects”) that offer reliable 100/100 Mbps broadband service to locations lacking at least 100/20 Mbps reliable service.

Funding Process
  • The program will operate on a reimbursement basis- making payments to awardees as they submit invoices for expenses incurred for actual work performed.  ​
Application Process and Timeline
  • Application requirements will be listed in the Program Handbook. The application process will include the following key steps:
    • Online Application (Deadline April 25, 2024)
      • Submit applicant information
      • Submit location data for each project seeking funding
      • Submit budget data for each project seeking funding
    • Location data for all applications posted online (May 15, 2024)
    • Curing (May 15 - 29, 2024)
      • Applicants with conflicting/competing locations may negotiate
      • If relevant, Applicants may revise and resubmit project details to reflect negotiations
    • Challenge Process/Public Comments (30 days beginning in June)
      • Applications are open to public comments and challenges
      • Challenge Process is described in the Program Handbook
    • Challenge Process Adjudication (July)
    • Application Evaluation and Scoring (anticipated mid-late August)
      • Department will evaluate all applications after Curing and Challenge Process conclude
      • See Program Handbook for Evaluation Criteria and scoring methodology
    • OBAC Review (October)
    • Intent to Award Announcements anticipated in November & December
    • Grant Agreement Negotiation​

    All dates current as of 10/31/24​

Frequently Asked Questions (Application Phase)
  • Q: As federal and state funding opportunities overlap, may a BDP grantee negotiate an awarded project that has already been awarded a federal grant?
    • A: The Department recommends that applicants only apply for projects that they intend to build if awarded a BDP grant. Please review the Handbook, Appendix B: Previously Funded Areas.
  • Q: Are matching funds required and, if so, is a grantee required to spend matching funds first before drawing down grant funds?
    • A: Matching funds are not required.
  • ​Q: Do state prevailing wage rates apply fo BDP-funded projects?
    • A: This determination must be made by the Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI). Please contact BOLI directly with any questions regarding prevailing wage. Click here for video recording of an introductory conversation on prevailing wage rates.​
  • Q: Should applicants submit one application that identifies multiple non-contiguous project areas or submit multiple applications that each identify a single project area?
    • A: Both are acceptable, though please note that multiple sub-projects in a single application will be considered as a single project for funding purposes.
  • Q: Do the Buy America Preference requirements for infrastructure projects apply to awards made under the ARPA/CPF program?
    • A: Awards made under the ARPA/CPF program are not subject to the Buy America Preference requirements set forth in section 70914 of the Build America, Buy America Act included in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, Pub. L. 117-58.
  • Q: Does the service cost to subscribers include taxes and fees when calculating for project scoring for affordability?
    • A: Yes. The cost of service is based on the price the consumers actually pay.
  • Q: If a municipality partners with an ISP, may the ISP submit a separate BDP application that identifies a separate project location? If yes, is it possible for both applications to receive awards?
    • A: Yes, to both.
  • Q: What types of broadband projects meet the definition of "regional scale" for BDP?
    • ​​A: A bonus score percentage will be given to applications seeking to close the Digital Divide at a regional scale, through unincorporated areas, and across city and/or county boundary lines, per BDP Handbook​, page 13.
  • Q: May we upload more than one file where we are permitted to “Choose a File" in the application?
    • A: No. Each section can only accommodate a single entry. If you have multiple responses to a given prompt, please consolidate them into a single PDF or .zip file.
  • Q: May we delete a previously uploaded file?
    • A: Any file previously uploaded can be replaced by toggling the “Upload a different file" checkbox to the right of submitted documents.
  • Q: What financial information are applicants required to provide?​
    • ​Per item E on pg. 16 of the BDP Handbook, applicants will be required to provide the last three years of app​​​licant’s audited or reviewed financial income statements, balance sheet, and cash flow statements. The Oregon Broadband Office will request financial information at a later date in the application process.​
  • ​​Q: If a grant awardee has partnerships in place for construction and​ equipment, are those items still required to be competitively bid out following the grant award?​
    • A: BDP grant recipients should refer to Uniform Guidance (2 Code of Federal Regulations Part 200) and additional CPF State Guidance for procurement requirements in acquisition of property or services on the broadband infrastructure projects.  More information can be found in the CPF State Guidance​ document and at this link https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/subtitle-A.
